title: Do SAE Probes Beat Random-SAE Baselines for Safety Concept Detection?

original_idea.body: Replicate the random-frozen-SAE sanity check on a safety-relevant detection target; compare trained-SAE, random-SAE, and direct linear probes; one open model.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: a sanity check on whether SAEs beat trivial baselines for safety detection informs heavy lab investment (level 4).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Three probe variants on a safety target with one open model; guided (level 4).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped with clear deliverable (trained vs random vs linear comparison) (level 5).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open model, no proprietary infra, externally valuable independent check (level 4).

low_compute.reasoning: Probe training + inference on open SAEs/model; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Random-baseline check exists generally; safety-specific replication partly open; partially addressed.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Safety-specific random-baseline replication may be partly open.
